2607.28023.title: Scaling, Lock-In, and Proxy Compliance: A Political Economy of Responsible AI
2607.28023.paper_summary: AI accountability at scale is an institutional problem: who can observe, verify, and change deployed systems. We develop a sequential political-economy model in which an AI vendor chooses auditability and substantive mitigation, a deployer monitors after adoption while facing switching costs, and enforcement depends on verifiable evidence. Anticipating the deployer's monitoring response, the vendor may stop at an observable procurement floor while mitigating below the social first best, producing a proxy-compliance equilibrium. We characterize the unique interior equilibrium and the corner in which harm is fully mitigated. Independent audit rights raise enforcement exposure directly; portability restores deployer leverage; incident reporting adds a regulator-visible evidence channel; and outcome-linked liability creates incentives that do not depend on vendor-controlled detection. The results explain why documentation and standardized evaluations can coexist with persistent post-deployment harms, and generate testable implications for monitoring, mitigation, and the gap between formal compliance and operational outcomes.
2607.28023.paper_summary_zh: AI 責任在大規模下是一個制度性問題：誰能觀察、驗證和改變已部署的系統。<lb/>我們開發了一個序列政治經濟模型，在這個模型中，AI 供應商選擇可審計性和實質性減輕措施，部署者在面對切換成本後進行監控，而執法取決於可驗證的證據。<lb/>預測部署者的監控反應，供應商可能會在可觀察的採購底線停止，同時在社會最佳情況下進行減輕，產生代理合規均衡。<lb/>我們描述了獨特的內部均衡和完全減輕傷害的邊界。<lb/>獨立的審計權直接提高了執法風險；可攜性恢復了部署者的杠杆；事件報告增加了一個監管者可見的證據渠道；而與結果相關的責任創造了不依賴於供應商控制的檢測的激勵。<lb/>這些結果解釋了為什麼文檔和標準化評估可以與持續的部署後傷害共存，並產生可測試的監控、減輕和正式合規與操作結果之間差距的含義。
